project.title_en: 大一 C 语言课程是否应该允许学生使用生成式 AI 编程助手？
project.question: 我们准备在大学一年级 C 语言课程中允许学生使用生成式 AI 编程助手。它到底会不会提高学习效果？应该怎样引入？

decision.decision_question: 大一 C 语言课程是否应该允许学生使用生成式 AI 编程助手？
decision.target_population: university first-year computer science students learning C programming for the first time
decision.target_context: 16-week lecture-lab course, 60 students, TA support, offline
supported_claims: AI coding assistants reliably increase task performance during training (completion speed, correctness) — E-001, E-006.
Unguarded generative AI access can harm independent problem solving when access is removed — E-004.
Guardrail design (hints instead of answers) substantially mitigates the negative learning effect — E-005.
Task performance gains do not automatically imply learning gains — E-004 vs E-006 (within-study contrast).
Tool capability is substantial: Codex solves roughly half to three-quarters of CS1 exam-style questions — E-010.
Professional-developer RCT shows ~55% faster task completion with Copilot; directness limited by professional population — E-008.
LLM code explanations rate comparable to student-authored explanations, viable as scaffold material — E-011.
uncertain_claims: Whether AI coding assistants improve or preserve actual programming learning in university novices — no direct university-level RCT in reviewed set [无直接证据]
Whether one-week neutral retention (Kazemitabaar 2023) extends to a semester — E-003.
Whether benchmark quality findings (E-009) and explanation-quality ratings (E-011) translate into classroom learning gains.
How comprehension/ownership difficulties documented in usability studies (E-012) behave over a full semester with guardrails.
contradicted_claims: The claim 'AI tools always improve learning' is contradicted by E-004 (unguarded access, -17% independent exam).
The claim 'speed gains equal learning gains' is contradicted by the task-vs-learning separation across E-001/E-006/E-008 vs E-004.
decision.reason_for_disagreement: Disagreement comes from outcome separation (task vs learning), tool design (guarded vs unguarded), and population (K-12 / professionals vs university). Task-performance evidence is consistently positive across randomized and benchmark studies; the only study measuring independent performance after AI removal shows harm without guardrails; usability and artifact studies add dependence and quality caveats rather than resolving the learning question.
decision.methodology_summary: Eight real sources: three randomized experiments (Kazemitabaar 2023 n=69 K-12; Bastani 2025 n≈950 high-school mathematics; Peng 2023 n=95 professional developers, preprint), one ESL writing mixed-methods study (Marzuki 2024), plus benchmark/capability/usability studies (Yetistiren 2023; Finnie-Ansley 2022; explanation-comparison 2023; Vaithilingam 2022). No direct RCT in university programming courses. Internal validity of the core RCTs is strong; directness to first-year university C programming is weak. All sources carry registry-verified DOIs (see benchmarks/doi-audit/report.md).

outcome_specific_findings.completion_time: positive during training and professional tasks (E-001, E-008)
outcome_specific_findings.assignment_score: positive during practice, negative on closed-book exam (E-004, E-006); tool itself scores passing-level on CS1 questions (E-010)
outcome_specific_findings.code_quality: mixed on benchmarks; security concerns documented (E-009)
outcome_specific_findings.metacognition: LLM explanations compare well (E-011) while novice ownership/debugging difficulties persist (E-012)
outcome_specific_findings.ai_dependency: documented crutch behavior with unguarded tool (E-004, E-005, E-012)

decision.short_term_effect: Task performance reliably increases; learning effect null-to-negative without guardrails.
decision.long_term_effect: No evidence beyond one week; long-term learning effect unknown.
decision.transfer_effect: No full transfer evidence; manual code-modification not harmed in one small study (E-002).
decision.risk_effect: AI dependency and over-reliance risk is real and documented for unguarded usage (E-004) and foreshadowed by usability findings (E-012).

applicability.suitable_for: pilot in first-year C course with guardrailed usage policy
applicability.not_suitable_for: unrestricted AI adoption without usage policy
required_conditions: guardrailed AI usage policy (hints not answers, modeled on GPT Tutor arm)

what_can_be_claimed: AI coding assistants raise task performance for novices during training.
Unguarded access carries a real risk of hurting independent problem solving.
Guardrail design can mitigate that risk.
Direct evidence for university C programming learning is missing.
Tool capability headroom is large (CS1 question pass rates; professional speed RCT).
what_cannot_be_claimed: AI coding assistants improve (or even preserve) university students' programming learning.
Any claim about which students benefit, based on university samples.
That benchmark or usability findings substitute for classroom learning outcomes.
missing_evidence: RCT of AI coding assistants in university programming courses with retention and no-AI transfer tests.
Studies varying AI usage policy within the same course.
Longitudinal data on AI dependency beyond one course.
Peer-reviewed replication of the professional speed RCT (Peng et al. remains a preprint).
decision.decision_rationale: Positive task-performance evidence plus documented unguarded-access risk, mixed quality/usability signals, and missing university-level learning evidence → bounded, guardrailed pilot with evaluation, not full adoption.
exceeds_evidence_boundary: Claiming 'AI coding assistants improve learning' exceeds the boundary: direct learning-effect evidence is missing.
Claiming 'AI works for everyone' exceeds the boundary: population and subject mismatch.

evidence.title: Studying the effect of AI Code Generators on Supporting Novice Learners in Introductory Programming
evidence.subject: introductory_python
evidence.population: 69 novices ages 10-17 with no prior text-based programming experience
evidence.claim: AI coding assistants significantly increase task completion speed and completion rate during training.
evidence.method: controlled experiment with random assignment, immediate post-test and 1-week retention test
evidence.title_zh: Studying the effect of AI Code Generators on Supporting Novice Learners in Introductory Programming
evidence.claim_zh: 在练习环节，无护栏的 GPT Base（类标准 ChatGPT 界面）使高中生的练习成绩相对对照组提高 48%，带护栏的 GPT Tutor 提高 127%（Table 1：practice 系数 0.137/0.361，对照均值 0.284）

evidence.title: Studying the effect of AI Code Generators on Supporting Novice Learners in Introductory Programming
evidence.subject: introductory_python
evidence.population: 69 novices ages 10-17 with no prior text-based programming experience
evidence.claim: Access to AI code generation did not decrease performance on manual code-modification tasks.
evidence.method: controlled experiment, code-modification task followed each code-authoring task
limitations: code modification is not full independent problem solving
evidence.title_zh: Studying the effect of AI Code Generators on Supporting Novice Learners in Introductory Programming
evidence.claim_zh: 移除 AI 访问后的无辅助独立考试中，GPT Base 组成绩比从未使用 AI 的对照组低 17%（统计显著），表明无护栏使用 AI 损害技能习得；机制上学生把 GPT 当'拐杖'直接抄答案（GPT Base 答对率仅 51%，其中 42% 逻辑错误、8% 算术错误），且学生自评过度乐观、未察觉学习受损

evidence.title: Studying the effect of AI Code Generators on Supporting Novice Learners in Introductory Programming
evidence.subject: introductory_python
evidence.population: 69 novices ages 10-17 with no prior text-based programming experience
evidence.outcome_measure: retention post-test one week after training
evidence.claim: One week after training, retention differences between Codex and baseline groups did not reach statistical significance.
evidence.effect: slightly better for Codex group but not significant
evidence.method: controlled experiment with delayed retention test
evidence.title_zh: Studying the effect of AI Code Generators on Supporting Novice Learners in Introductory Programming
evidence.claim_zh: 带护栏的 GPT Tutor（教师设计提示而非直接答案）在练习成绩 +127% 的同时，移除访问后的独立考试负效应基本消除（-0.004，不显著），说明精心设计的护栏可兼得练习提升与学习保持

evidence.title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
evidence.subject: mathematics
evidence.population: nearly a thousand high school math students in Turkey
evidence.outcome_measure: exam without access to AI resources after practice phase
evidence.claim: Students with unguarded GPT-4 access performed 17% worse on the independent exam than the control group, despite higher practice performance.
evidence.method: large-scale randomized controlled trial, practice phase then closed-book exam
evidence.title_zh: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
evidence.claim_zh: 训练阶段使用 OpenAI Codex 的 10-17 岁新手在 45 道 Python 代码编写任务上表现显著提升：完成率提高 1.15 倍、得分提高 1.8 倍

evidence.title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
evidence.subject: mathematics
evidence.population: nearly a thousand high school math students in Turkey
evidence.outcome_measure: exam without access to AI resources after practice phase
evidence.claim: Guardrail design of the AI tutor (hints instead of answers, teacher-informed prompts) largely eliminated the negative learning effect.
evidence.effect: negative effect essentially eradicated, no positive effect observed
evidence.method: large-scale randomized controlled trial, three arms
evidence.title_zh: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
evidence.claim_zh: 训练期使用 Codex 的学习者一周后评估后测成绩略好于对照组，但差异未达统计显著（保持力无显著差异）；Scratch 前测高分者若有 Codex 使用史，保持后测显著更好

evidence.title: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
evidence.subject: mathematics
evidence.population: nearly a thousand high school math students in Turkey
evidence.outcome_measure: practice problem performance during study sessions
evidence.claim: Access to GPT-4 during practice improves task performance (48% for GPT Base, 127% for GPT Tutor) — but this task performance does not transfer to independent exam performance.
evidence.method: randomized controlled trial with practice and closed-book exam phases
evidence.title_zh: Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics
evidence.claim_zh: 质性案例研究中，3 名 EFL 学生珍视 ChatGPT 的辅助价值（消除不确定性、澄清词汇、提供内容建议、语法/结构反馈，让学生专注于创意层面），并形成语言精修、观点生成与结构、校对与信心增强等使用策略

evidence.title: Impact of ChatGPT on ESL students' academic writing skills
evidence.subject: academic_writing_esl
evidence.population: undergraduate ESL students at an Indian university
evidence.claim: ChatGPT as a formative feedback tool produced a significant positive impact on students' academic writing skills with positive student perceptions.
evidence.effect: significant positive impact on writing skills
evidence.method: mixed methods intervention study, pre/post/delayed tests and focus groups
evidence.title_zh: Impact of ChatGPT on ESL students' academic writing skills
evidence.claim_zh: 同一质性研究中，学生担忧 AI 使用的学术真实性与过度依赖风险（建议过于复杂/正式、语气不符、文化刻板印象等局限），强调必须保持人的判断并寻求教师/同伴反馈，呼吁伦理指引与批判性思维培养

evidence.title: The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
evidence.subject: standardized_javascript_http_server_task
evidence.population: 95 recruited professional developers completing a standardized coding task on a freelance platform
evidence.claim: Professional developers with Copilot access completed a standardized coding task about 55% faster than the control group (RCT, n=95).
evidence.effect: ~55.8% faster task completion in Copilot group
evidence.method: online randomized controlled experiment with objective completion-time metric
evidence.title_zh: The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
evidence.claim_zh: 随机对照实验（n=95）显示：使用 Copilot 的职业开发者完成标准化编程任务的用时比对照组缩短约 55%。

evidence.title: GitHub Copilot AI Pair Programmer: Asset or Liability?
evidence.subject: code_generation_benchmarks
evidence.population: Copilot-generated and human-written programs drawn from published benchmark datasets
evidence.claim: Systematic benchmark evaluation reports mixed quality results for Copilot-generated code relative to human code: correctness competitive on parts of the benchmark while security-relevant defects are documented.
evidence.effect: mixed quality profile; no single-direction summary
evidence.method: systematic empirical evaluation of generated code against human baselines on public benchmarks
evidence.title_zh: GitHub Copilot AI Pair Programmer: Asset or Liability?
evidence.claim_zh: 系统性基准评估显示 Copilot 生成代码相对人类代码的质量结论不一：部分正确性具竞争力，同时记录到安全相关缺陷。

evidence.title: Using GitHub Copilot to Solve Introductory Programming Problems
evidence.subject: introductory_python
evidence.population: CS1 exam-style question sets answered by Codex and compared against published student score distributions
evidence.claim: Codex produced passing-level solutions for roughly half to three-quarters of CS1 exam-style questions depending on the dataset, indicating substantial task-capability headroom available to novices.
evidence.effect: passing solutions on ~50-75% of questions across datasets
evidence.method: capability benchmark against published student distributions; reproducible question sets
evidence.title_zh: Using GitHub Copilot to Solve Introductory Programming Problems
evidence.claim_zh: Codex 在 CS1 考试风格题目上能给出通过水平的解答（依数据集约 50%–75%），表明新手手中存在可观的任务能力余量。

evidence.title: Comparing Code Explanations Created by Students and Large Language Models
evidence.subject: code_explanation_scaffolding
evidence.population: Student-produced versus LLM-produced explanations of short programs under controlled comparison
evidence.claim: Controlled comparisons find LLM-generated code explanations comparable to (in places better than) student-authored explanations, suggesting viability as explanatory scaffold material rather than as a replacement for student explanation practice.
evidence.effect: comparable-or-better rated quality vs student explanations
evidence.method: controlled comparison with blind rating of explanation pairs
evidence.title_zh: Comparing Code Explanations Created by Students and Large Language Models
evidence.claim_zh: 受控比较发现 LLM 生成的代码讲解与学生自撰讲解相当（部分更优），适合作为解释性支架材料，而非替代学生的解释练习。

evidence.title: Expectation vs. Experience: Evaluating the Usability of Code Generation Tools
evidence.subject: programmer_usability_of_codegen_tools
evidence.population: 24 participants in a within-subjects usability study of Copilot-style tools
evidence.claim: Despite faster first-task completion, participants struggled to understand and debug AI-generated solutions and reported low ownership of the final program - documenting metacognitive and dependence risks that pure speed metrics miss.
evidence.effect: documented comprehension/ownership difficulties despite speed gain
evidence.method: within-subject usability study with tasks, observation and interviews
evidence.title_zh: Expectation vs. Experience: Evaluating the Usability of Code Generation Tools
evidence.claim_zh: 尽管首任务完成更快，参与者难以理解并调试 AI 生成的解法、对最终程序所有权感低——记录了纯速度指标遗漏的认知与依赖风险。

intervention.target_learners: university first-year C programming students (60-student lecture-lab class)
learning_goals: independently write and debug small C programs without AI
understand core concepts: variables, conditionals, loops, arrays, pointers
use AI tools critically as explanation and debugging aids, not answer machines

phase_1.name: Phase 1 — Independent Foundation
activities: first 2 weeks of assignments completed without any AI code generation
phase_1.ai_usage_rule: full code generation forbidden; AI allowed only for conceptual explanations

phase_2.name: Phase 2 — Explain, Don't Solve
activities: weeks 3-4: AI allowed to explain errors, concepts and debugging approaches
phase_2.ai_usage_rule: AI may explain but must not produce full solutions

phase_3.name: Phase 3 — Structured Collaboration
activities: weeks 5-7: AI allowed to generate partial code; students must explain every AI-generated block in their own words
phase_3.ai_usage_rule: partial code generation allowed; mandatory written explanation of key logic; submission requires reasoning trace
phase_3.outcome_check: weekly lab completion and code-quality rubric

phase_4.name: Phase 4 — Transfer Check
activities: week 8: new programming task completed in a no-AI environment
phase_4.ai_usage_rule: no AI access during transfer assessment
phase_4.outcome_check: transfer test score, independent problem solving

intervention.ai_usage_policy: AI usage is allowed in three explicitly graded modes (explain / collaborate / no-AI-transfer). Copying unexamined AI output is an academic integrity violation and is assessed via the reasoning-trace requirement.
intervention.teacher_role: design guardrailed prompts and rubrics; monitor usage logs; hold weekly reflection debriefs
intervention.student_role: complete assignments in the allowed mode; submit reasoning traces; reflect on when AI helped vs. when it masked understanding
intervention.reflection_requirement: students must explain key AI-generated logic in their own words; one written reflection per phase
intervention.assessment: no-AI baseline quiz, mid-pilot quiz, no-AI transfer task, code-quality rubric, AI-usage self-report
risk_control: guardrailed usage policy modeled on Bastani 2025 GPT Tutor (hints, not answers)
no-AI transfer assessment prevents grade inflation from task-performance gains
usage logs reviewed weekly to detect crutch behavior
stop_conditions: transfer-test scores drop significantly below baseline cohort expectations
widespread integrity violations in reasoning traces
AI dependency signals exceed threshold in risk metrics

evaluation.research_question: In a first-year C programming course, does a guardrailed AI coding assistant (explain-only → structured collaboration) improve independent problem solving without increasing AI dependency, compared to no-AI instruction?

groups.treatment: two lab sections using the 4-phase guardrailed AI policy
groups.comparison: two matched lab sections without AI access (same instructor and materials)

evaluation.baseline: week-1 no-AI programming quiz (independent problem solving, completion time)
evaluation.post_test: week-8 no-AI programming quiz (independent problem solving, code quality)
evaluation.retention_test: final exam (week 16) — delayed measure 8 weeks after pilot
evaluation.transfer_test: week-8 novel programming task in a strictly no-AI environment
process_metrics: AI usage logs: prompts submitted, copied blocks, reasoning traces
risk_metrics: AI dependency index (usage without understanding, from reasoning-trace quality)
false confidence (post-quiz confidence vs actual score)
evaluation.analysis_plan: pre-registered comparison of treatment vs comparison sections on baseline-adjusted learning metrics (ANCOVA); task-performance metrics reported separately from learning metrics; subgroup analysis by prior programming competency; stop-condition monitoring at weeks 3, 5, 7.
evaluation.success_threshold: treatment group shows non-inferior independent problem solving (delta within 5%) AND superior or equal retention AND AI dependency index below threshold; if independent problem solving declines >10%, the pilot is judged unsuccessful regardless of task-performance gains.
stop_conditions: AI dependency index exceeding pre-set threshold for two consecutive weeks

decision_zh.decision_question: 大一 C 语言课程是否应该允许学生使用生成式 AI 编程助手？
decision_zh.target_population: 首次学习 C 语言编程的大一计算机专业学生
decision_zh.target_context: 16 周讲授课+实验课，60 人班级，助教支持，线下
supported_claims: AI 编程助手在训练期间可靠地提升任务表现（完成速度、正确性）—— E-001、E-006。
无护栏的生成式 AI 访问在移除工具后可能损害独立问题解决能力 —— E-004。
护栏设计（给提示而非给答案）能大幅缓解负面学习效应 —— E-005。
任务表现提升并不自动等于学习提升 —— E-004 与 E-006 的研究内对照。
工具能力可观：Codex 能解出约半数至四分之三的 CS1 考试风格题目 —— E-010。
职业开发者 RCT 显示 Copilot 带来约 55% 任务提速；但职业人群限制直接性 —— E-008。
LLM 代码讲解的质量评级与学生自撰讲解相当，可作支架材料 —— E-011。
uncertain_claims: AI 编程助手能否真正改善或保持大学新手的编程学习——本证据集中没有大学层面的直接 RCT [无直接证据]
Kazemitabaar 2023 的一周中性保持性能否延伸到一个学期 —— E-003。
基准质量结论（E-009）与讲解质量评级（E-011）能否转化为课堂学习收益。
可用性研究所记录的理解/所有权困难（E-012）在整学期护栏条件下会如何演变。
contradicted_claims: 'AI 工具总能提高学习'被 E-004 反驳（无护栏访问，独立考试 −17%）。
'速度收益等于学习收益'被 E-001/E-006/E-008 与 E-004 之间的任务-学习分离所反驳。
decision_zh.reason_for_disagreement: 分歧来自结果分离（任务 vs 学习）、工具设计（有护栏 vs 无护栏）与人群（K-12/职业者 vs 大学生）。随机实验与基准研究中任务表现证据一致为正；唯一测量移除 AI 后独立表现的研究显示无护栏时有害；可用性与工件研究补充依赖与质量警示而非解决学习问题。
decision_zh.methodology_summary: 八个真实来源：三项随机实验（Kazemitabaar 2023，n=69，K-12；Bastani 2025，n≈950，高中数学；Peng 2023，n=95，职业开发者，预印本）、一项 ESL 写作混合方法研究（Marzuki 2024），以及基准/能力/可用性研究（Yetistiren 2023；Finnie-Ansley 2022；讲解对比 2023；Vaithilingam 2022）。无大学编程课程的直接 RCT。核心 RCT 内部效度强；对大一 C 语言情境的直接性弱。所有来源均带注册表核验 DOI（见 benchmarks/doi-audit/report.md）。

outcome_specific_findings.completion_time: 训练期与职业任务中为正（E-001、E-008）
outcome_specific_findings.assignment_score: 练习期为正、闭卷考试为负（E-004、E-006）；工具本身在 CS1 题目可达通过水平（E-010）
outcome_specific_findings.code_quality: 基准上结论不一；记录到安全隐患（E-009）
outcome_specific_findings.metacognition: LLM 讲解对比占优（E-011），而新手理解/所有权困难仍存（E-012）
outcome_specific_findings.ai_dependency: 无护栏工具下记录到拐杖行为（E-004、E-005、E-012）

decision_zh.short_term_effect: 任务表现可靠提升；无护栏时学习效应中性偏负。
decision_zh.long_term_effect: 无超过一周的证据；长期学习效应未知。
decision_zh.transfer_effect: 无完整迁移证据；一项小样本研究中手动代码修改未受损（E-002）。
decision_zh.risk_effect: 无护栏使用的 AI 依赖与过度依赖风险真实且有记录（E-004），可用性发现亦予印证（E-012）。

applicability.suitable_for: 在大一 C 课程以护栏化使用政策开展试点
applicability.not_suitable_for: 无使用政策的全面放开采用
required_conditions: 护栏化 AI 使用政策（给提示不给答案，仿 GPT Tutor 组）

what_can_be_claimed: AI 编程助手在训练期提升新手任务表现。
无护栏访问存在损害独立问题解决的真实风险。
护栏设计可以缓解该风险。
大学 C 语言学习的直接证据缺失。
工具能力余量大（CS1 通过率；职业提速 RCT）。
what_cannot_be_claimed: AI 编程助手能改善（乃至保持）大学生的编程学习。
基于大学样本的任何『哪些学生受益』结论。
基准或可用性发现可替代课堂学习结果。
missing_evidence: 在大学编程课程中带保持与无 AI 迁移测试的 RCT。
同一课程内变化 AI 使用政策的研究。
跨越一门课的 AI 依赖纵向数据。
职业提速 RCT 的同行评审重复（Peng 等仍为预印本）。
decision_zh.decision_rationale: 任务表现的正面证据 + 有据可查的无护栏风险 + 混合的质量/可用性信号 + 大学层面学习证据缺失 → 有界、护栏化、带评估的试点，而非全面采用。
exceeds_evidence_boundary: 『AI 编程助手提高学习效果』—— 超出边界：缺少直接学习效应证据。
『AI 对所有人都有效』—— 超出边界：人群与学科错配。

measurement_policy: No pooled effect or mean is computed by Studio. Missing values remain null.
